draft.title: The early Republic
card: The Qing dynasty fell in 1912 after the Xinhai Revolution of 1911. China became a republic, ending about 2000 years of imperial rule.
Sun Yixian was the first provisional president. He soon handed the presidency to Yuan Shikai, a powerful general who commanded the strongest army in the north.
Yuan ruled as a strongman. He weakened the elected parliament and the Nationalist Party, and in 1915 he moved to make himself emperor.
Many people opposed the plan, including provincial leaders and generals, and Yuan gave it up. He died in 1916. The Republic had not united China or built lasting institutions.
draft.remember: The Republic began in 1912, but Yuan's grab for power left it weak and China divided.

a.q: Which action by Yuan Shikai most clearly worked against the idea of a republic?
opts: Trying to make himself emperor in 1915
Taking over the presidency from Sun Yixian
Commanding the strongest army in northern China
Dying in office in 1916 with no clear successor
a.why: A republic is not ruled by an emperor, so Yuan's attempt to take the throne went against it directly. Becoming president was part of the Republic's own arrangements, since Sun handed the office over, so it is not the clearest attack on the idea.
a.clue: Think about which title a republic does not have.

b.q: Why did Yuan Shikai's years in power leave the early Republic weak?
opts: He weakened parliament and faced wide opposition to his plan
He let the elected parliament take over many of his powers
He gave up the presidency soon after Sun Yixian chose him
He united China under strong and lasting new institutions
b.why: Yuan weakened parliament and the Nationalist Party, then lost support when he tried to become emperor. This left the Republic with few lasting institutions. The Republic was not weakened by too much parliamentary power, because Yuan worked to reduce it.
b.clue: Ask what Yuan did to parliament and how people reacted to his emperor plan.

a.best: Trying to make himself emperor in 1915

b.best: He weakened parliament and faced wide opposition to his plan

problems.detail: The clue ('Ask what Yuan did to parliament and how people reacted to his emperor plan') restates the two halves of the right option, so a student can match it without knowing the idea.
The clue ('which title a republic does not have') points straight at the only option naming a title a republic lacks (emperor). That makes the question trivial for Year 12.
